fields.Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "Following the Alignments", "body": "Michelle Gibson dates her own research to 2016, when she noticed North American cities falling along straight lines, extended those lines, and recognized the shape of a star tetrahedron. She says about nineteen or twenty spreadsheets now hold the places that sit on her circles and global alignments. Earlier grounding came from Drunvalo Melchizedek's work, sacred geometry and the Flower of Life during her years in Fairbanks, and from the Megalithomania conference she first attended in 2011. She started with a flat map, switched to a globe, and insists the alignments drove the conclusions rather than any prior theory."}, {"title": "Old World Architecture", "body": "Michelle Gibson argues the evidence sits in everyone's home town: courthouses, libraries, schools, theaters and museums, plus prisons and asylums she says were used through the nineteenth century to warehouse adults and children. Chance Garton offers the asylum beside his own house, a castle dropped into a city for no obvious reason, and his Springfield, said to be built on three star forts for a Civil War that found a town already standing, above a tunnel network only the rich and large corporations can enter. She credits the Shrine Mosque to the Moors rather than its official 1923 story."}, {"title": "The Moorish Umbrella", "body": "The spine of Michelle Gibson's screen share is the Ouachita Empire, which she calls an ancient matriarchal civilization of the Ouachita Moors, surviving only in place names like the Ouachita Mountains and Lake Ouachita, with Monroe, Louisiana as its imperial seat and Poverty Point a major center. She spells Moors as Muurs to tie them to Mu, also known as Lemuria, and treats Phoenician, Persian, Mughal and Tartarian as regional names under one Moorish umbrella. Laying the Mississippi Delta beside the Nile Delta, she reads the straight channels in both as the work of a canal-building civilization. Chance Garton adds the Egyptian-style temples reported in the Grand Canyon."}, {"title": "Artificial Time", "body": "Chance Garton frames the false matrix as a problem of artificial timekeeping: there is no such thing as seven in the morning, no such thing as Tuesday, and the only measure is the moon running new moon to new moon. Michelle Gibson answers that old buildings were lined up to the full moon and the equinoxes, and describes a Mayan calendar of day signs and tones meshing like cogs in a wheel. She believes the linear system was brought in to trap us in a year circuit, that the timeline and the Earth's grid were hijacked, and that dates like 3/22 and 9/11 carry ritual weight for the controllers."}, {"title": "Worldview Healing and the Reset", "body": "Chance Garton sets worldview healing as the day's agenda and asks near the end of the free hour how the research healed hers. Michelle Gibson answers that love wins and God wins, that the controllers could never have come in without our consent and had to make us think it was our idea, and that now is the time to take our power back, since everything spirals out of our personal energy. In his solo outro Chance floats the cosmic egg, a cosmology of concentric ring lands that expands outward, and wonders whether mud is new land emerging and whether the Great Reset crowd is hijacking an ancestral memory."}]
fields.Intro Paragraph 1: The official narrative says our cities were built by horse-and-buggy pioneers, but the "Mudflood" evidence points to a far more advanced, global civilization that was systematically erased.
fields.Intro Paragraph 2: In this episode, Michelle Gibson (Piercing the Veil of Illusion) joins Chance Garton to decode the hidden infrastructure of the Old World. From the Washitaw Empire in North America to the sophisticated canal systems mirrored across the globe, we unveil the secret resets that redefined our reality.

fields.Plus Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "The Mud Flood and the Dug Out City", "body": "Michelle Gibson frames the mud flood as whatever removed the original civilization from the surface, allowing that it could have been one cataclysm or a series, black magic or an engineered event such as a Carrington style flare or an earthquake strong enough to liquefy solid ground into mud. Her sharper claim is that the nineteenth century was excavating rather than building, that the infrastructure already existed and was only being made functional again so a new economy could profit from it. Half buried doors and windows in Natchez, downtown Springfield and Prescott become the same evidence repeating everywhere."}, {"title": "A Time Loop Between 1492 and 1942", "body": "Gibson's own theory is a three dimensional time loop anchored on 1492, the year Granada fell, and 1942, the year she assigns to the Philadelphia Experiment, with 1717 sitting as the exact midpoint two hundred and twenty five years from either end. She points out that 1717 is also the founding year of the premier Freemason lodge in London and of New Orleans, which she calls a star city. The conversation then pauses on the number eighty eight long enough to note that eight by eight is sixty four, and leaves the rest for listeners to ponder."}, {"title": "Following the River to Monsanto and Coca-Cola", "body": "Tracing river towns up the Mississippi, Gibson lands on the Monsanto brothers of Natchez, a slave trading family out of Spain whose name means Holy Mountain, and on John Francis Queeney, who married into that family and founded Monsanto Chemical in St. Louis in 1901, naming it for his wife's people. The first product was saccharin. Upriver she finds Joseph Biedenharn, the first bottler of Coca-Cola, whose crop dusting fleet became Delta Airlines in 1928. Chance Garton reads Bayer's sixty six billion dollar purchase of Monsanto as the executives cashing out ahead of the lawsuits."}, {"title": "Wars and Weather as Demolition Work", "body": "Gibson's position is that the wars and weather events of the modern era were aimed at destroying the old grid, star forts especially, and she offers a Vicksburg castle with a moat that the Union Army destroyed before the site became an artillery battery. Chance Garton supplies the pattern he keeps noticing in the photographs: Civil War ruins, the San Francisco earthquake, the Great Chicago Fire and the West Coast wildfires all leave masonry pulverized to dust while the wooden power poles are still standing, which points him toward a hidden technological component rather than cannon fire."}, {"title": "Schumann Spikes and an Optimistic Turn", "body": "Chance Garton closes the extension by asking about the Schumann resonance and the wild spiky activity of the previous couple of weeks. Gibson says she does not track it closely but reads it as light coming in, recalling Gregg Braden's framing of it around 2010 as the heartbeat of the Earth. From there she argues that humanity is a hologram of source, that this is precisely why the energy has been worth harvesting, and that the planners got uncomfortably far in their implementation before we remembered we are the ones we have been waiting for."}]

fields.Plus Quotes JSON: [{"text": "In order to receive new information, you have to let go of what you've been taught to believe is true, especially where history's concerned.", "author": "Michelle Gibson", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/e0694c15-c073-4a98-b7b4-e53efaa54f8a/MICHELLE-GIBSON.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "I think we're talking about all of the stuff that we're told was being built was actually being dug out of this mud flow.", "author": "Michelle Gibson", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/e0694c15-c073-4a98-b7b4-e53efaa54f8a/MICHELLE-GIBSON.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "There's some weird overlap between what seem like disconnected events that maybe point to the fact that there's a hidden technological component to these various forms of destruction.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/aa717e55-9487-4255-a7df-3f8ef10940c4/Chance+Garton+Patreon+Portrait.png?content-type=image%2Fpng"}, {"text": "I really do think golf courses are a cover-up of mound sites.", "author": "Michelle Gibson", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/e0694c15-c073-4a98-b7b4-e53efaa54f8a/MICHELLE-GIBSON.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "You can build these crazy structures, but you can't build a road first? How are you even getting the bricks in here?", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/aa717e55-9487-4255-a7df-3f8ef10940c4/Chance+Garton+Patreon+Portrait.png?content-type=image%2Fpng"}, {"text": "So Bayer is Monsanto now, doing the same thing.", "author": "Michelle Gibson", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/e0694c15-c073-4a98-b7b4-e53efaa54f8a/MICHELLE-GIBSON.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "Everything you see with new eyes becomes fascinating, and it's just way better than swallowing that blue pill from the agents of the Matrix.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/aa717e55-9487-4255-a7df-3f8ef10940c4/Chance+Garton+Patreon+Portrait.png?content-type=image%2Fpng"}, {"text": "I think that's all wars have been, is this cover story to get rid of key targets.", "author": "Michelle Gibson", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/e0694c15-c073-4a98-b7b4-e53efaa54f8a/MICHELLE-GIBSON.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "I've speculated that the Philadelphia Experiment was a time travel deal, and I have heard that Aleister Crowley was involved in the Philadelphia Experiment, and I don't trust that guy at all.", "author": "Michelle Gibson", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/e0694c15-c073-4a98-b7b4-e53efaa54f8a/MICHELLE-GIBSON.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "As holograms of source, we have the potential for everything, but there's a lot more harmony than there is dissonance in nature.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/aa717e55-9487-4255-a7df-3f8ef10940c4/Chance+Garton+Patreon+Portrait.png?content-type=image%2Fpng"}]
